advisories.title: humanfs: Recursive copy follows symlinked files and copies data from outside the source tree
advisories.exposure: ESLint uses humanfs for repository traversal. The vulnerable recursive-copy API requires a copy operation over attacker-controlled symlinks; these scripts do not call that API. It was patched rather than exempted.

advisories.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
advisories.exposure: The test UI/API and redirect-mock route can handle attacker-controlled URL paths when the test server is listening. test:ui is an advertised command, so this was treated as reachable server tooling, not dismissed because tests are development dependencies. The advertised test:ui command starts the affected server. An attacker reaching its API is the stated file-read/execution precondition; loopback alone is not considered a fix. The patched UI and real loopback HTTP endpoint were verified.

advisories.title: ajv has ReDoS when using `$data` option
advisories.exposure: ESLint loads Ajv for configuration/schema checks. The ReDoS advisory requires the $data option and adversarial schema/data; this repository uses a checked-in flat TS config and does not enable $data. A compatible patch was still installed.

advisories.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
advisories.exposure: Tailwind content discovery/watch loads braces via micromatch and chokidar. Deep attacker-controlled glob patterns can exhaust the stack. Current patterns are fixed tracked strings (tailwind.config.js), not gallery input or file contents; no pattern-input API exists in the app. This remains an unresolved high advisory, not harmless tooling.
advisories.fixed_version: No published fixed braces version. Registry latest is 3.0.3; advisory covers <=3.0.3.

advisories.title: Browserslist: Unbounded memory growth (no cache eviction) via distinct query results, leading to eventual OOM
advisories.exposure: Autoprefixer/build processing loads Browserslist. Distinct adversarial queries or a malicious browserslist-stats.json trigger the cache/prototype paths; no custom statistics file or user-controlled query is present. Long-lived dev/build tooling can still be exposed by changed project configuration; patched within the existing major.

advisories.title: postcss-selector-parser allows denial of service through uncontrolled AST recursion
advisories.exposure: Tailwind/PostCSS/typography can parse CSS selectors supplied by repository source. Untrusted PR CSS or imported project styles can trigger CPU exhaustion during build; this is a real build-input exposure. Some parents still constrain parser 6.x, so the remaining advisory is not declared resolved.
advisories.fixed_version: 7.1.6; retained Tailwind/PostCSS/typography constraints also install 6.0.10/6.1.5. The earlier 6.1.0..<6.1.3 recursion issue was patched in affected 6.1.5 nodes.

advisories.title: Rollup 4 has Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal
advisories.exposure: Application/library builds execute Rollup output generation. The write-path advisory needs attacker-controlled output filenames/path construction; output paths here are tracked vite.config.ts values. Build plugins or untrusted source/configuration can widen exposure. Patched to a fixed 4.x release.

advisories.title: Tinypool: Prototype Pollution gadget in worker options leads to Remote Code Execution
advisories.exposure: Vitest 3 normal test runs execute this worker pool. The RCE gadgets require prototype pollution plus affected worker/run options; no pollution source was demonstrated in project tests, but the affected worker operation is used in CI. Vitest 4 removes this dependency entirely, avoiding an incompatible override of Vitest 3's ^1.1.1 constraint.
advisories.fixed_version: 2.1.2 fixes both pool advisories, but Vitest 3 declares ^1.1.1 and no fixed 1.x exists. Repair: Vitest 4.1.11 removes tinypool.
